newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF sees 1997 profit, sales growth.
newsitem.headline: BASF sees 1997 profit, sales growth.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Thursday that its objective of increasing earnings in 1997 and achieving group sales of more than 50 billion marks was within reach.
"Following the customary lull during the vacation period, we expect sales and earnings to continue at a high level in the coming months," BASF said in a statement.

"Strong demand for our products and appropriately full order books confirm these growth expectations. At present, we consider our objective of increasing group sales in 1997 to over 50 billion marks and exceeding the previous year's earnings to be within reach."
BASF made the forecast as it announced a 3.4 percent rise in net income to 1.417 billion marks in the first six months of 1997 from 1.370 billion in the year-earlier period.
Pre-tax profit rose 5.8 percent to 2.458 billion marks from 2.323 billion, at the lower end of market expectations.
Sales in the period rose 14.5 percent to 27.8 billion marks from 24.3 billion.
